executions.summary: Inspected README.md and all HarborQueue source/tests without modification. The mandated 13-test suite passed. Independent Node built-in probes confirmed dependency scheduling, the three-slot ceiling, no concurrent duplicate execution, bounded/blocked work behavior, cancellation and physical-slot retention, checkpoint rollback before rename, recovery as interrupted plus a unique retry, live-owner exclusion, graph-error rejection, and normal per-attempt result/error recording. Correctness is nevertheless not fully demonstrated: scheduler.cjs:11-13 and :143 silently discard nested non-JSON payload members (a function-valued property was accepted and vanished from memory and disk), contrary to README.md:48. Also, validateState at scheduler.cjs:73-83 accepts internally inconsistent per-attempt history: a completed job with currentAttemptId referencing a still-running attempt was accepted unchanged, and two attempts for one job with duplicate number 1 were accepted. These gaps can hide malformed recovery state and make attempt history unreliable.

executions.summary: The documented invariants are not all correct. Inspection covered README.md, scheduler.cjs, scheduler.test.cjs, server.cjs, index.html, and test/dashboard.test.cjs. Existing tests demonstrate cancellation behavior, checkpoint rollback/fail-closed handling, ordinary recovery, three-slot enforcement, graph validation, and per-attempt history. However, scheduler.cjs lines 388-397 contain a stale-lock TOCTOU race: multiple processes can read the same dead-owner record, then one process can delete the replacement live lock created by another. Deterministic Node-only probes produced two simultaneous owners with different tokens and two concurrent executions of the same durable job with distinct attempt IDs. This violates exclusive ownership and permits duplicate execution beyond the documented intentional crash-recovery semantics. The existing ownership test checks only rejection of an already-live lock and does not exercise concurrent stale-lock reclamation.

executions.summary: Verified the stale-lock correction and crash-recovery invariants. Acquisition serializes contenders with an exclusive guard and re-reads the lock under that guard before any removal. The deterministic child-process barrier showed one owner and one job execution while the replacement owner remained alive; the delayed contender rejected without removing its lock. Dead-owner recovery completed one retry, and an abandoned acquisition guard failed closed while preserving the ordinary lock. README.md documents the required manual guard-removal procedure. No source files were modified.

tests.evidence: Exit code 0. All 3 focused tests passed. The race test observed only contender A starting and ending, one durable history entry, and contender B rejecting because A was live. Recovery marked the crashed attempt interrupted and executed exactly one replacement attempt. The abandoned guard produced the documented manual-intervention error and left the dead-owner lock unchanged.

tests.command: Static inspection of scheduler.cjs:375-488, scheduler.test.cjs:248-343, test/ownership-contender.cjs, and README.md ownership semantics
tests.evidence: The pre-guard stale read is used only for deterministic fault injection. After acquiring <file>.lock.acquire, the implementation authoritatively re-reads the current lock and removes it only when its current PID is dead. Guard cleanup verifies the token; cleanup failure fails acquisition and releases only a token-matching owned lock. README.md documents that interrupted guards are not automatically reclaimed and require operator verification before manual removal.
